title: US equity, options and bond markets closed — New Year's Day (Friday 2027-01-01, the holiday that makes 2026-12-31 the year's last session)
source: NEWS: three primaries, all RE-FETCHED DIRECT 2026-09-09 by this event's own initial research rather than inherited from the proposing lane. (1) nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars (HTTP 200 after its 302, 109,180 bytes): the New Year's Day row parses cell by cell as ['Thursday, January 1', 'Friday, January 1', '—*'] for 2026 / 2027 / 2028, so 2027 is a full closure on Friday January 1 with no observance shift. Footnote * reads verbatim 'Because the holiday falls on Saturday, January 1, 2028, no New Year's Day holiday is observed' — the contrast that proves the 2027 cell is a real observed closure and not a formatting artifact. (2) sifma.org/resources/guides-playbooks/holiday-schedule (HTTP 200, 299,272 bytes): the U.S. panel's 'New Year's Day 2026/2027' card gives a full US fixed-income close on 'Friday, January 1, 2027' with 'Early Close (2:00 p.m. Eastern Time): Thursday, December 31, 2026'; the U.K. and Japan panels carry the same 2027-01-01 full close, and the Japan panel additionally lists a 'Bank Holiday / Thursday, December 31, 2026'. (3) www.optionseducation.org/api/expirationcalendar (HTTP 200, 34,871 bytes) marks 2027-01-01 {"holiday":{"description":"Exchange/OCC holiday","hatched":true}}. That marker is load-bearing rather than decorative because the same file's own vocabulary reserves hatched 'Exchange/OCC holiday' for full closures and uses an unhatched 'Bank holiday' label for the bond-only days when equities stay open — verified across all 36 holiday rows it carries for 2025-2027: 30 hatched, and exactly 6 'Bank holiday' (2025-10-13, 2025-11-11, 2026-10-12, 2026-11-11, 2027-10-11, 2027-11-11), every one a Columbus or Veterans Day. CROSS-CHECK RUN THIS SESSION: the OCC's 10 hatched 2027 holidays and NYSE's 10 2027 table rows agree one-for-one on all ten dates, two independent primaries with zero disagreement. Reproduced by statute and weekday arithmetic: 5 U.S.C. 6103 fixes New Year's Day on January 1, and January 1 2027 is a Friday, so it is observed on the day. Filed estimate on the two standing counts every sibling closure entry documents: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for an exchange's or a trade association's own holiday calendar, and this lane may not self-confirm. The DATE is not in doubt — the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research (docs/research/events/new-years-day-market-closure-2027-01-01.md), which read the one prior proposal first per EVENT-RESEARCH.md — proposals/new-years-day-market-closure-2027-01-01.from-christmas-market-closure-2026-12-25.json, filed 2026-09-08 — and then re-fetched every primary rather than inheriting any of them. The proposal's date, sources and reasoning all reproduced; it is now shadowed and inert. WHY IT EARNS A ROW: this closure is what makes Thursday 2026-12-31 the LAST SESSION OF 2026 rather than the second-to-last, a fact at least seven tracked entries dated 2026-12-31 depend on. THE MEASURED FINDINGS THIS LANE ADDS, all computed 2026-09-09 from CBOE VIX_History (9,268 rows) and a Yahoo ^IXIC session record (9,241 sessions, 1989-12-27 to 2026-09-08) because FRED's fredgraph endpoint was EGRESS-BLOCKED from this runner. (a) THE SESSION-BUDGET MIRROR: the same Friday holiday that gives December 2026 22 sessions / 140.0 equity hours — the 1990-2025 record MAXIMUM, per the christmas-market-closure-2026-12-25 ledger — gives January 2027 19 sessions / 123.5 hours, TYING THE 1990-2026 MINIMUM. Every one of the five prior Januaries that opened on a Friday New Year's Day ran 19 or 20 sessions (1993:20, 1999:19, 2010:19, 2016:19, 2021:19). Budget the pair, never either alone. (b) THE CORRECTION TO THE SIBLING LEDGER: christmas-market-closure-2026-12-25 names its measured post-break VIX rise a 'turn-of-year vol re-mark'. Reproduced here on an independent session record — its +4.32% 3-day-gap break print (16/20) and +8.30% four-session convergence (30/36) both replicate EXACTLY — but the four-session window it measures ends inside December in 36 OF 36 YEARS and never once crosses New Year. The re-mark is CHRISTMAS-SPECIFIC and spent by year-end. (c) THE NEW YEAR BREAK IS A NULL IN AGGREGATE: VIX across the year-end gap runs -0.20% mean, median -0.79%, 16 of 35 years positive, the 52nd percentile of all 9,229 one-session VIX moves since 1990 — a coin flip. The gap-length split survives (+2.66% on 3-non-trading-day gaps, 8/14, vs -3.61% on 1-day gaps, 5/16) but at half Christmas's reliability. The exact 2026/27 analogue — a Friday January 1 — is +7.62% mean and 4 of 5 up, and n=5 with a -7.56% to +18.55% range is not a number anything may be sized on. (d) THE EQUITY LEG IS A NULL BOTH WAYS: Nasdaq across the New Year break is +0.15% mean, 19/35. (e) NEW YEAR'S DAY IS THE ONLY US MARKET HOLIDAY DROPPED RATHER THAN SHIFTED WHEN IT FALLS ON A SATURDAY, proved mechanically from the session record: Dec 31 WAS a trading session in all 4 Saturday-January-1 years (1994, 2005, 2011, 2022), while July 3 was NOT a session in both Saturday-July-4 years (2015, 2020) and Dec 24 was NOT a session in both Saturday-Christmas years (2010, 2021). 4/4 against 4/4 — which is why NYSE footnote * drops 2028 entirely and a sibling lane reaching 2028 should expect no entry for it. Low impact and it stays low: a scheduled closure known 114 days ahead moves no price, licenses nothing, symbols is empty, and no house playbook is calendar-keyed. Kind sector, symbols empty and status estimate reuse the settled precedent every US trading-hours entry on this calendar follows.
